This study extends the Poisson autoregressive model (ARPO) to allow for time-varying coefficients, resulting in a new variant called TEDPAC. While the original ARPO model has been found to be difficult to estimate due to boundary issues, the new variant overcomes this limitation by incorporating time-dependent parameters. Additionally, a smoothing method is presented to estimate the varying coefficients, building on the theoretical properties of the model. Monte Carlo simulations and an application to daily stock theft data demonstrate the effectiveness of the variant and its underlying estimation techniques.

While using photometry as a method for aerosol optically thin measurement may have been considered unconventional, particularly in the astrophysical community, our group has adapted it effectively for monitoring air quality over extensive areas, even in low-resolving signal scenarios. As a result, we have been able to achieve precise aerosol vertical profile measurements using wide-field stellar photometry as well as broad-band wide-field photometry. As well, we have been capable of recovering the Scattering Angles of light and even clearing conditions from the data obtained. As a result, the method is found to be similar to lidar technology but without the cost and complexity associated with it, making it an inexpensive alternative for monitoring purposes. While the method may have been limited by atmospheric conditions such as wind and turbulence, particularly when using wide-field photometry, overall it is considered to be a valuable tool especially in emergency situations involving accidents or natural disasters. As well, the data obtained is found to be compatible with that of aerosol sensors and radar systems but with enhanced resolving power at lower frequencies.

Numerous numerical methods fall under the umbrella of Langevin Dynamics, each tailored to address specific simulation requirements. Our work presents a one-step implicit numerical scheme, characterized by second-order accuracy, specifically designed for stochastic differential equations governing molecular dynamics with state-dependent noise. Our analysis demonstrates the method's stability through linear stability analysis and achieves a large acceptance rate through optimal tuning of the time step in tests with both harmonic and anharmonic potentials. Furthermore, our research produces high-quality molecular sampling, as evidenced by smooth power spectra in simulations of a 1D oscillator and a peptide configuration, demonstrating the effectiveness of our numerical approach.

Image description systems have seen a significant leap in performance over the past few years, according to evaluations conducted with human participants. This progress has sparked the proposal of implementing real-time human-based assessments to evaluate the output of these systems. Before drawing conclusions about the effectiveness of image description generators and their contrast with human performance, it is crucial to first examine the quality of the data used in existing studies. A thorough investigation of the literature revealed that many claimed instances of miscommunication were not backed up by concrete evidence. Furthermore, when we analyzed reported discrepancies between system outputs and human judgments, the results were surprisingly low, contradicting the notion that current image description systems have a high rate of errors. In response to these findings, there is a call for higher standards in reporting results, the development of more comprehensive and unambiguous evaluation metrics, and the creation of a gold-standard dataset specifically tailored for research purposes on the evaluation of image generator outputs.

We resolve how specific infinity-dimensional equation systems relating differential operators conformally transform can lead to generating functions for critical exponents in four-dimensional quantum field theory, specifically in beta-function computations for scalar fields with spin 0,1,2. These equations, termed spinor-photon-electron or SPE for brevity, are part of an infinite-dimensional class of homogeneous equation systems with polynomial solutions. The derivation of SPE's spin and mass generating functions involves recognizing solutions to local, infinity-dimensional equation systems, local and global, finite-dimensional and infinite-dimensional manifold solutions to these equations. The derivation proceeds by establishing an infinite-dimensional conformal field framework, where the SPE equations are interpreted as curvature constraints, yielding an infinite-dimensional conformal gravity theory with dynamical symmetry.

In 1935, Pauli proposed a principle that no two fermions can occupy the same quantum state, now recognized as a cornerstone of physics. Building on this foundation, we extend the concept to bosons, a previously unexplored idea. By analyzing the radiation curve of a blackbody and the particle distribution in the universe, we predict that non-degenerate fermions and bosons outside of extreme conditions have negligible impact on observable properties like pressure and density. However, we acknowledge that exceptional conditions, such as those found in stellar interiors, could potentially cause low-energy particles to become degenerate, prompting a re-evaluation of the principle mentioned earlier. Moreover, we suggest that highly exotic scenarios, including those involving dark stars and black holes, might lead to novel states of matter with significant pressure, possibly contributing to the dark matter observed in the universe.

This article presents the ISW-OFDM technique, a modified version of OFWD-OFDM, specifically designed for systems with only one receive antenna. In scenarios involving a large number of data streams, this method reduces the complexity of solving optimization problems by utilizing only one carrier frequency and an beamforming pattern with linear phase changes across multiple antennas. This approach effectively minimizes Inter-Carrier Interference (ICI) and enables diversity gain through multiple antennas and OFDM symbols. Simulation results demonstrate that ISW-OFDM performs similarly to traditional OFDM in cases with a low number of data streams, but slightly worse in scenarios with a high number of data streams.

We present a framework suitable for fitting experimental data on semi-inclusive deep
ly inelastic scattering using parton distribution functions (PDFs) and describe its implementation within the ROOT environment. Our proposed, conceptually
clear hierarchical Bayesian approach enables a seamless integration of theory, experimental data, and physical constraints, facilitating a statistically
robust inference process. We apply this methodology to a simple example using the CT18 NFT18 parton fitting framework and generate fitted PDFs and their
covariance matrix in the ROOT format for demonstration purposes.

This study undertakes a linear analysis of a methane-air jet flame's response to acoustic fluctuations, factoring in turbulence and flame instability linearized equations, with the aim of forecasting flame instability in rocket engines. Unlike previous studies, our model takes into account the interaction between acoustic fluctuations and turbulence, as well as the impact of turbulence on flame instability, utilizing an active flame model that computes flame surface curvature-induced instability in real-time. Unlike prior approaches, we do not assume a constant extinction rate. Instead, we simulate the impact of turbulence and flame instability on the reaction rate using the LES framework, factoring out acoustic fluctuations' influence via a linearized KNS equation for real-time analysis. To validate the model, we utilize high-speed video and gas concentration data to tune and verify it, resulting in accurate predictions of the flame's behavior under varying flow conditions. Our findings demonstrate the model's capacity to accurately depict the impact of acoustic fluctuations on flame instability, setting the stage for the integration of control measures to mitigate instability in future studies.

Nonlocal gravity theory is reformed in a vector-tensor framework, enabling a clear comparison with conventional vector-tensor theories. In this modified representation, the theory can be described using only vector-tensor quantities, eliminating the need for bi-form variables. Within this'material'vector-tensor description', the theory's nonlocal characteristics are expressed in terms of operational definitions involving the integration of vector-tensor constitutive relationships. Nonlocal gravity theory is also translated into an equivalent generalization of Einstein gravity theory, the (linear) metric theory, where integral operaters are demonstrated to be operative, allowing for a'metric'constitutive relation'equivalent to the nonlocal bi-form equation in the nonlocal theory.

Compact heavy ion colliders can facilitate the study of quantum phase transitions in quark-gluon plasma by enabling heavy ion-electron collisions.  In proton-electron colliders, electron posits can trigger the creation of small ion systems like $^{7}\mathrm{Li}$, which are effective in producing quark pairs, and thereby allow for the investigation of the transition from weak to strong interaction.  These small ion systems are advantageous in such studies due to their low multiplicity and near-central collision conditions.  However, their rare occurrence makes the process difficult to observe in large heavy ion colliders like those at the LHC.  To address this challenge and explore the feasibility of using small heavy ion systems at a future high-energy heavy ion collider like FHLC, simulations were conducted with the HIINGLE model.  The model's results indicate that even at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 100$ TeV, the production of $D\bar{D}$ mesons in central collisions of $^{10}\mathrm{B}+^{10}\mathrm{B}$ would be too low for effective measurement.

Observations of some variable sources within the Milky Way's center that have shown no outbursts in over a decade have led some researchers to suggest the source of certain gravitational waves detected by LIGO. However, this conclusion may conflict with findings about the behavior of neutron star binaries. Our analysis of recent studies reveals that the variability patterns of these binaries can be explained by a combination of factors without requiring long periods of random quiet phases. One key element involves the alignment of magnetic fields between the neutron star and its companion, while another may involve the neutron star's internal structure and its effect on outburst dynamics.

Bipartite graphs representing connections between distinct user groups are increasingly used to analyze real-world data. A common challenge in these graphs is compressing edges by merging equivalent users within each group. This paper addresses the reverse problem, where graphs are expanded to incorporate new users. This type of graph modification is valuable for customization in applications like recommendation systems. The difficulty of this customization task is established, but a more efficient solution is presented using a parameterized approach. The complexity of this approach is proven to be linear in the solution size, and a 2-hardness proof is provided for a specific problem variant. The significance of this work lies in the relatively low hole size of the solution, highlighting the practical feasibility of customizing large-scale graphs in real-world scenarios.

Recent studies in energy harvesting have shown that underutilized segments of the CPU can be used to power active attacks like glitching.  However, these methods require complex hardware modifications that are difficult to implement.  In contrast, our approach uses the already available dynamic voltage and frequency adjustment capabilities of the CPU to conduct active attacks.  By systematically reducing the CPU's clock speed, we found that even significant frequency reductions do not adversely affect the success of our approach.  Through benchmarks conducted on the Spectre v1 attack, we observed that Spectre view1 can be executed successfully by initially executing the vulnerability at normal frequencies and then continuing the attack at reduced speeds.  Furthermore, we were able to generate an optimal strategy for energy harvesting that maximizes the size of the area in which the approach can be executed.  In experiments conducted on Skylake and Ivy Bridge processors, we found that our method can be used to harvest energy effectively across a wide range of frequencies, enabling active attacks in areas previously considered inactive.

A novel link rearrangement technique, termed the $\times$-move, is introduced and proven to be equivalent to the conventional disintegration method in welded link theory. The $\times$-move addresses non-planar crossings distinct from the standard over/under information captured in welded link theory. By addressing this shortcoming, the document establishes an upgraded version of the traditional disintegration procedure, the $\star$-theorem. The $\star$-theorem incorporates both standard over/under data from welded link diagrams and additional details revealed by the $\times$-move.

Synchronization is crucial for cooperative tasks among distributed systems of robots. This paper explores how to design a coordination strategy to improve synchronization accuracy over a robot network engaged in cooperative activities. The design of an optimal synchronization policy that maximizes accuracy is derived, along with its closed-form expression. The policy's benefits over uniform time synchronization methods are demonstrated through theoretical analysis and numerical simulations. Further exploration reveals the trade-offs between synchronization accuracy, the probability of intervention, and the duration of observation. The paper concludes that strategic synchronization benefits the network of robots by improving accuracy without additional computation or communication capabilities, or extended observation times, over uniform methods.

In woven theory, wrench representations hold special significance due to their use in establishing group regularities and in creating dynamic wrench representations for infinite groups like the diagonal-square-brace group. Our new wrench format, encompassing both existing formats plus additional transformations, enables a proof that Bruck-Bernstein groups regularity applies and yields a dynamic representation for this specific group. Our innovative wrench depiction is shown to be equivalent to woven theory's wrench format and the Bruck-Bernstein group representation, while offering advantages over these existing formats.

The detection capabilities of advanced gravitational wave detectors are hindered in the high-frequency range by the quantum limitations of measurement and signal loss within optically isolated mirror systems. Overcoming this constraint is critical for identifying gravitational waves generated by binary neutron star mergers. We present the concept of the sloshing Sagnac interferometer, a novel topology that can extend the sensitive frequency range of the detectors. Through a linearized model of this new topology, we've imported the signals detected by the LIGO interferometers to analyze the benefits of various signal recycling configurations and mirror suspension setups in reducing signal loss. The results indicate that the sloshing Sagnac interferometer can achieve an improvement in high-frequency sensitivity equivalent to the benefits of increasing the total power by a factor of 10, without additional power amplification. Additionally, we propose that implementing low-loss mirrors would yield gains similar to adding 10 meters of effective arm length. Based on our simulation of the detector's sensitivity, the sloshing Sagnac topology is predicted to have performance comparable to expanding the laser wavelength to 850nm and enhancing the total power by 10 times, or improving the main detector's arm length by a factor of two. These benefits can be realized with existing technology. However, to fully realize the potential of third-generation detectors with higher sensitivity and better detector response, innovative topologies like the sloshing Sagnac interferometer are necessary.

Improved image quality in optimizing resource allocation for green multi-cellular networks with backhaul limitations requires a mention; instead; enhanced protocol performance in 'Listen-Schedule-Report' and 'Report-Schedule-Listen' has significance.

Neural language models have largely surpassed $N$-gram models due to their superior efficiency and performance. However, we find that $n$-gram models still hold significant value, especially in high-throughput text generation tasks. Given the quick ability of $n$-gram models to estimate language probability and sample from the language space, we propose a framework that combines them with a neural network's refined predictions in a 'residual' learning approach. Our experiments show that by integrating the strengths of both models, we can achieve faster prediction and generation speeds while also enhancing overall language understanding. Specifically, our optimized versions of BERT and T5 that use the $n$-gram model framework, called BibERT and BibT5, demonstrate remarkable results on various text creation tasks, surpassing even the best-performing neural models. Moreover, our findings reveal that residual learning is more effective than standard training approaches in achieving better outcomes.

This investigation in殷的 language focuses on Informed Optical Character Identification, or iOCR, an enhanced version of the existing i211 standard.  The primary objective of 殷的 project is to improve the accuracy of ballot tallying systems, particularly when used in conjunction with machine voting terminals.  The underlying algorithm consists of three main sections: preprocessing, where the system divides images into manageable chunks and removes unnecessary characters such as graphs and recurring letters; a deep learning component based on Long Short-Term Memory networks; and a posteriori smoothing that utilizes the Eckman-Harless theorem to reduce errors. The accuracy of 殷的 project was evaluated through a set of tests employing various methods of misclassification evaluation, including random, recurrent, and context-aware errors.  The results demonstrate that iOCR significantly outperforms the existing standard, with 99.70% overall accuracy compared to 99.08% for i211.  The benefits of 殷的 project are particularly notable when it comes to multiple-choice questions, with 99.92% accuracy compared to 99.74% for the existing system.  The research findings are also discussed in the context of statistical significance measures, such as the kappa coefficient.

A simplified computer model is used to simulate and document various global atmospheric circulation patterns in Mars-like atmospheres with scintillation lengths between 2 and 30 meters and gravity similar to Earth's. These simulations, with total atmospheric pressure ranging from 0.3 to 3 bar and wind velocity resolution from 0.5 to 10 m/s, allow us to examine how wind velocity, atmospheric mass, and atmospheric conditions interact to determine circulation patterns with time scales of 0.5 to 2 seconds. In atmospheres with low vertical movement, three main regions are found near the equator: large-scale circulation cells, jet streams, and areas of rapid rotation. As wind velocity increases, the shape of these circulation cells changes from a U-like to an inverted L-like form, with the return air currents shifting from mid-latitudes to higher latitudes. In very rapid conditions exceeding 20 m/s, a new circulation cell may emerge at the poles. Three primary circulation patterns are observed in atmospheres with low vertical movement: cyclostrophic, hybrid, and geostrophic. The distribution of these patterns is influenced by atmospheric conditions, pressure, and wind velocity. Notably, super-rotation of days is possible in very rapid conditions with low pressure, whereas weeks-long patterns are common in slower conditions with higher pressure.
This study formulates two integral integral expressions to represent the reciprocal gamma function, confirming their validity through numerical verification.

Our research develops a hierarchical approach called the HR functionals method to address the many-body Schrödinger equation for Bose gases in a continuous space environment. In this framework, a level-0 HR functional corresponds directly to the Schrödinger equation for a single Bose gas, while higher levels represent interactions between additional gases. By exploiting the probabilistic properties of Poisson processes, we can link infinite levels of this hierarchy to the ideal Bose gas. This allows us to approximate the Schrödinger equation for interacting Bose gases through a statistical sampling process. Furthermore, we can derive an approximate dynamics known as the PH rate equation from this hierarchy, which also features a level-0 functional associated with the ideal Bose gas and higher levels reflecting interactions between additional gases. Through this process, we can obtain an approximation for the many-body operator in an interacting Bose gas system by means of a truncation, leading to the development of a random quantum hydrodynamic model called the RQHD. This model can be defined at the level-m and is capable of solving the rate equation mentioned earlier. To enhance the stability of this model, we implement a smoothing technique known as the Gaussian Wigner transform, resulting in a regularized version called the RGW hydrodynamic model. Finally, we can utilize a probabilistic phase-space representation of quantum states to simulate the system's evolution through this hierarchical framework.

The surge in available knowledge has made it crucial for embedded systems to efficiently filter and acquire information from vast sources. The Instructor-Student (I-S) neural architecture, consisting of an Instructor network and a Student network, has shown improved performance in knowledge distillation between disparate systems. The I-S approach's modular design allows for both batch and interactive I-S modes, with research demonstrating the I-S neural architecture's ability to facilitate knowledge learning and expand an I's training beyond the initial Student model. The following survey examines the I-S neural architecture, categorizing I-S methods into three types: Student-centric, Instructor-centric, and Shared models, and explores various I-S strategies. Furthermore, the article discusses the I-S approach's application in diverse knowledge domains, such as optical character recognition, visual recognition, and verbal recognition, summarizing key findings and potential future directions.

Graphical models are a powerful statistical tool with complex likelihood functions that present challenges for efficient inference. Many efficient inference methods exist, but their high space and time complexity can be significant, especially in large-scale or strongly connected scenarios, where exact maximum probability estimand and constrained optimization can be computationally expensive. We introduce a simple and efficient approach for exact inference that outperforms existing methods by an order of magnitude in a specific case, by using a new compact function representation.

Recently introduced is a higher rank algebra known as the Racah algebra $R(n)$. A special variant, termed the special Racah algebra $sR(n)$, is then defined as a quotient of the Racah algebra by its central elements. It is then demonstrated that this $sR(n)$ algebra is equivalent to the centralizer $Z_{n}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ through application of classical invariant theory, particularly with respect to a specific embedding of the Lie algebra $U(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ within a tensor product. As a result, a particular sequence of polynomial algebras, referred to as the Hil-Poincaré sequence, is recognized as representations of the special linear algebra through a series of quotients. Additionally, a closed-form expression is derived for the generating function of these algebra representations, utilizing a method of factorization associated with the Racah algebra. As a byproduct, a recursive relation is obtained for the derivation of this expression, particularly through the use of a differential operator acting upon a polynomial algebra.

The paired permutation test is a non-parametric method used to detect correlations between variables by shuffling data. It's particularly effective in high-dimensional settings or when dealing with unusual data patterns that violate standard assumptions. However, as the data set size increases, the computational requirements for paired permutation tests become prohibitive due to the large number of required shuffles. In contrast, a paired paired-permutation test, which is an efficient algorithm that recoves correlation between variables by swapping blocks of data between sets, can be completed in linear time. This test is particularly well-suited for use in online applications with large data sets. The paired-permutation test has been shown to be as accurate as the standard permutation test in maintaining proper error rates when evaluated both before and after the data sets are shuffled. In order to enhance the test's accuracy in detecting correlations, a structured method that considers the relationship between deleted and kept data when shuffling blocks can be used. This test has been found to be particularly effective in detecting correlations between variables when compared to the standard paired-permutation test.

Through several initiatives including rescaling of baryon chemical potential, changing initial energy densities, modifying the initial velocity fields, varying initial radiuses and changing junction order in simulations, we reconstructed the data from Au+Au, Cu+Cu and Ni+Ni collisions at various centralities and energy levels at RHIC.  Through the iPMTs model's phase randomization at the beginning of the simulation, directional flow harmonics of different orders were produced in higher centralities and different energy levels, mirroring the increases seen in Experiments at central collisions and peripheral collisions respectively.  By varying initial radiuses and centralities in simulations, different $v_1/n$ to $\langle\epsilon_n/\epsilon_1\rangle$ relationships were observed in Au+Au and Cu+Cu collisions at different centralities, with a more pronounced curvature in more central collisions, similar to what's observed in Experiments. This study develops a Poisson multi-Bernoulli mixture (PMBM) filter where target birth locations are represented on a grid. A key advancement features an efficient prediction step that leverages only a portion of the grid points. By utilizing a compact set of hold-over models combined with probabilistic assignments for unmonitored grid points, the new method achieves more precise and non-uniform tracking. This enhancement is particularly beneficial in active sensor management systems, allowing for optimized resource allocation. A simulated scenario demonstrates the application of the improved filter in a mobile robot's tracking task, controlled by a 2D phased array of sensors.

The dynamics of soccer games include sudden changes and significant events that referees can't instantly resolve, creating opportunities for teams to outmaneuver their competition. In these pivotal moments, our team's robot soccer system can gain an advantage through quicker decision-making capabilities. A specific request by the French team in a RoboCup challenge led to the development of a new scarified state-space compression technique, utilizing deep reinforcement learning to make exceptional decisions during games. Our proposed method demonstrates its effectiveness through simulated games, showcasing its ability to outperform an existing approach in certain scenarios while also proving its viability through successful RoboCup game simulations.

This study explores the principles behind using single-point laser Doppler velocimetry (LDV) sensors to measure velocity profiles over extended areas. By leveraging a remote measurement technique called image displacement, we can obtain a two-dimensional velocity profile at a distant point within a fluid flow, without requiring a large and complex probe setup. A key challenge addressed in the study is ensuring that the observation points for the LDV sensors have a common measurement region, which is often difficult due to the curvature of laser beams over long distances. To overcome this, we propose an optical arrangement that utilizes flat mirrors to create a common measurement point, allowing for expanded area measurements. The effectiveness of this setup is validated through experiments conducted on a flowing water channel, demonstrating the potential benefits of using single-point LDV sensors for large-scale flow research.

We provide explicit expressions for the operators representing the posited operator's spectrum's eigenvectors corresponding to the eigenvalues at the origin's vicinity. These eigenvectors are posited to be the only ones in that particular area. Additionally, we determine the precise characteristics of the spectrum's eigenvalues further removed from the origin's vicinity.

In experiments observing beauty particle decays, the Belle II experiment is a side-angle scan initiated by the Belle experiment, the Belle experiment observed the decay of $D_s$ particles where an axion-like particle and a photon were produced alongside another beauty particle, involving the oscillation of $B-\bar{B}$ particles. The experiment data consisted of 10^8 Belle II events, a factor of ten improvement over the Belle experiment's 10^9 events observed. A side-angle enhancement factor of 100, applicable to the Belle II experiment, results in sensitivity improvements equivalent to the Belle experiment's observed capabilities. The experiment analysis yielded no observation of specific axion-like particles, enabling the determination of minimum coupling strengths for specific particles where a coupling length exceeds a specific angle of one or two radians, applicable to the Belle II experiment and a factor of one to ten more restrictive than current observations of 10^9 beauty particles. A future observation of at least 10^10 events is projected to yield an observation of specific axion-like particles similar to what the Belle experiment has already achieved.

Our findings from three distinct semantic change detection tasks reveal the limitations and possibilities of using contextual language models. These tasks, which involve identifying differences in meaning between lines of content, are highly relevant in creating adaptive systems that provide updated information. As a start, we evaluated several contextual methods, including average and attention-based approaches along with various pre-trained models, on three datasets of changed pairs of text. Following that, we conducted three rounds of experiments: contextual models were used to train classifiers for each pair, then a bootstrap method was employed to further enhance the results. Building on that, we designed and conducted a large-scale experiment with 100 test pairs of content, which allowed us to analyze the performance of the systems in distinct scenarios. The results indicate that contextual language models excel in identifying significant changes in meaning but are highly susceptible to noise from grammatical differences. As a solution, we tested a combination strategy that uses both conceptual and discursive analyses to improve the overall performance of the system. On theChinesedataset of 800 pairings, this approach yielded better results than using either method separately. The findings from our study contribute new insights into the application of contextualization techniques for semantic alteration detection and highlight the complexity of the task. This may pave the way for more extensive conceptual changes in evaluation and dataset creation in the future.

This method focuses on the possible asymmetry in spin alignment of heavy jets, including quasars, observed by AGNs. A potential clue to axion mass ranges from this technique emerged when analyzing existing data, revealing possible Asymptotic Giant Branch star observations could contribute to determining low-mass axion parameters. Quantum harmonic oscillators were used to provide a clear and detailed example for investigating non-equilibrium situations. A specific setup was set up where a force is applied gradually and then kept constant, to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed path integral method. Using this setup, various observables were calculated precisely with the revised simulation approach, showing its capability to produce accurate results by comparing outcomes to established analytical solutions.

We develop an approach to application of Hoare logic in the context of quantum programs, incorporating expectation values into the predicate used, and then verify the program's correctness based on the modified logic.  This method relieves the burden on programmers of ensuring the validity of postconditions in the form of operators or projections, and instead allows for the use of scalar-valued expectation values as preconditions and postconditions in correctness assertions.  By utilizing this relational logic, it facilitates the verification of common quantum operations such as state preparation, measurement, and unitary evolution, and even more intricate sequences of actions.  We demonstrate the richness of this modified logic through a set of non-trivial examples, and support it with a formal derivation of the relationship between traditional and relational hoare logic, incorporating the maqre toolkit for automated verification.

The paper addresses the issue of polarization signal bias that persists in vector magnetic field maps derived from observations of the effect known as the Zeeman splitting.  In response to the growing demand for 3D magnetogram data in solar physics research, a precise method is required to identify the source of this bias and a model-based approach is proposed to correct it.  Following the consideration of the complexity of magnetic structures on the surface of the Sun, a simple linear fit to the observed polarization signals is found to be insufficient to accurately reflect the true magnetism distribution.  The research identifies the source of the bias and provides a model-based solution to mitigate its impact.

Over the course of history, both groups and their collections of involutions have formed various structures including permutations, multipartite graphs, and bipartite graphs. We've developed a theoretical framework that views the lattice of boolean structures as a collection of parts within a bigger picture of a bidimensional diagram of types. By conducting a in-depth examination of this specific subset, we've constructed a boolean structure defined for the bidimensional diagram of classes. This new lattice of subsets serves as a foundational framework for a defined boolean decomposition, demonstrating its significance in the study of group theory.

This research paper defines and discusses the concept of Bertrand curves within the context of loxodromic manifolds equipped with a semi-metric structure. A notable example of such a curve type is found in physics, specifically in the study of particle dynamics on spacetime manifolds. A curve is classified as a Bertrand curve when there's a relation between its position and a related curve's position, along with a consistent relationship between their local angular measurements. The paper explores the conditions required for a curve on a manifold to be considered a Bertrand curve, finding that rank conditions on the angular relation are necessary. Furthermore, it is demonstrated that on strict time-like surfaces, a 'first order' condition is not sufficient, with a specific example provided where a curve's angular measurement follows a constant pattern but does not qualify as a Bertrand curve. Based on these insights, a new condition is proposed: a curve is a Bertrand curve if its relationship with a related curve is defined by constant angular and radial measurements.

The choice of loss function for a neural network is widely regarded as a key decision with far-reaching implications, given the numerous loss functions developed to date, making it crucial to understand its impact on model performance, particularly in deep learning contexts. This research aims to investigate the connection between final classification accuracy and the chosen loss function, utilizing the extensive capabilities of deep learning models, and explores the potential for optimizing performance by selecting or designing loss functions, or optimizing their hyperparameters, as well as the feasibility of creating new classes based on the output of existing loss functions, and finally, it will optimize the hyperparameters of the optimization method that yields the best results.

Our dataset of logical rules, comprising nearly 100k principles across 28 categories and spanning 7 domains, has been utilized to train and evaluate artificial intelligence systems that automate decision-making.  These systems, a type of recursive module-based learner, require the processing of text-derived information to infer hidden attributes from observable ones.  We employed a sophisticated, three-stage training methodology to teach these systems to perform reasoning tasks.  Initially, we trained the models on identifying straightforward characteristics such as categories and sources using supervised learning.  Subsequently, we extended this training to include the discovery of recursive features like syntax and semantics.  Finally, we utilized this knowledge to facilitate if-then reasoning within our models.  To test our systems, we created three distinct reasoning benchmarks, resulting in two new datasets, "FeaRea" and "Thou", with notable success rates of 84.9% and 82.2% respectively, particularly in complex scenarios.  In comparison to previous learners, our models outperformed them in revealing conditional information.  However, we found that training data requiring diverse characteristics was more challenging to process.  Our findings contribute to the field of automated learning and decision-making, providing insights into how systems train and evaluate on logical rules, and revealing the challenges of discovering conditional attributes.  This information is valuable for researchers in machine learning and artificial intelligence, especially those interested in reasoning, module discovery, and training strategies.  It also benefits practitioners

Our proposed framework addresses the challenges encountered by robotic systems in fast-paced and dynamic environments. Since these systems operate in real-time and deal with high-dimensional data, they require efficient methods for processing and predicting video streams. We propose a dual representation consisting of a summary and a predicted future video frame, which our robotic system uses to make predictions. We've developed an online learning algorithm to choose informative frames to use as summaries and deep neural networks to build the dual representation. Using multiple real-world datasets, including ones used in previous research, we've shown the effectiveness of our framework for predicting video streams in high-dimensional spaces.

A graph's full metric dimension is calculated based on identifying the smallest set of vertices that allow for the shortest paths to be uniquely determined for all other vertices. Although this concept is well-established, implementing it can be challenging in practical situations, particularly when dealing with large graphs where the set of unique identifying vertices is also large. To address this challenge, we propose a variation of the full metric dimension called the trimmed metric dimension, which is calculated by removing the longest path from the graph before determining the smallest set of unique identifying vertices. We provide a formula to calculate the trimmed perimeter for finite graphs and explore how this value changes in response to alterations in the graph's structure and perimeter.

This study aims to improve the accuracy of heart sound categorization, specifically for detecting crackles, by exploring innovative preprocessing techniques. The research considers both convolutional and additive noise reduction methods, as well as the impact of using compression formats like WAV and FLAC. A unique dataset is utilized, consisting of heart sound recordings with and without noise, allowing the researchers to evaluate the effectiveness of various preprocessing methods. The results show that additive noise has a more significant impact on accuracy compared to convolutional noise, with the best results achieved when using the original, uncompressed recordings. The study finds the effectiveness of noise reduction methods varies depending on the specific scenario, with spectral methods outperforming filtering methods in certain cases. The research also highlights the importance of proper preprocessing techniques in medical data analysis and the potential use of MLL-based models for heart sound classification.

We analyzed the production of the 83 and 99 micron fine structure lines of neutral atomic carbon in spiral galaxies using molecular gas mass-resolving spectroscopic data. These lines, which result from metastable states decaying to the ground state, were found to be unexplainable by conventional radiative transfer models that consider only these transitions. However, a proposed solution involves low-energy shocks or gas turbulence causing some of these excited states to transition to even lower energy levels, effectively trapping them. This process, when implemented in simulations that also include this downscattering transition, was found to accurately predict observed line strengths. Its implications suggest that these far-infrared lines could be useful for determining molecular gas densities, especially in the outer regions of galaxies where traditional methods fall short. Additionally, it is proposed that in the molecular gas outer reservoirs, predominantly low-energy collisions between H2 and Ci are responsible for line production, rather than typical star formation-related shocks.

We identify the precise state conditions under which a ASEP line process becomes stationary, particularly highlighting its application to a velocity ASEP model in a multi-lane configuration. By leveraging the line process definition, we determine the precise velocity specifications required for the multi-lane ASEP model to achieve a steady state.

This study examines various mathematical models developed in response to the ongoing pandemic to support public health communication and policy-making. Although model selection should ideally be influenced by the specific context of the pandemic at hand, including data availability and research goals, a survey of existing studies reveals that compartmental models, particularly SEIR-based variations, have been the most extensively utilized and well-documented in the current pandemic in comparison to other types of models such as agent-based, network, and fractional calculus models. While reports on the underlying dynamics of the epidemic, its epidemiological characteristics, and its epidemiological forecasting predominate, the analysis also identifies studies exploring the epidemic's treatment options, control measures, asymptotic behavior, origin of outbreaks, as well as the impact of misdeclaration and changes in transmission rates. Although the article is focused on the current pandemic, the resulting framework is applicable to other infectious disease outbreaks as well. Given the specific circumstances of the ongoing epidemic, policy-making and public health communication are recommended to incorporate real-time data visualization, real-time forecasting, and the underlying mechanism of the epidemic's dynamics in order to enhance their effectiveness.

Determining whether galaxy structure or bulge size influences the star formation main sequence break is still debated. This study aims to clarify the role of galaxy structure in creating the turnover at the end of the star formation main sequence by analyzing local, massive star-forming galaxies through a Bayesian meta-analysis of HST images and SPHEREX spectra. A key factor identified is the correlation between bulge mass and central star formation rate, not total galaxy mass, that trends downward as star formation meta-persistence decreases. Additionally, a positive relationship exists between bulge mass and meta-persistence, not galaxy mass, that's observed. A hypothetical model demonstrating the connection between the downturn in central star formation meta-persistence and the departure from the star formation main sequence is presented, supporting the idea that spiral galaxies with large bulges and rapid star formation in the center are rare due to the gravity of massive bulges, causing tidal forces during galaxy interactions that result in outflows and the cessation of star formation. However, when considering the vast number of galaxies with small bulges and low central star formation rates, the gravity of the dark matter halo is found to be the primary cause of meta-persistence outflows in these massive galaxies with low star formation rates, not just the bulge. The research suggests that as galaxies grow through mergers and grow their bulges, the role of dark matter halo forces is replaced by the regulation of central star formation rates and the formation of outflows in massive, star-forming galaxies

This paper explores cross-lingual sentiment analysis, investigating the
potential for pre-trained models and a many-shot setting.  We find that directly
utilizing pre-trained models in the few-shot setting yields poor results.  To
overcome this challenge, we propose a novel multi-task learning framework that
simultaneously performs sentiment analysis and finds parallel comments across
languages.  Our experiments on Facebook posts in English and Hindi demonstrate
that our proposed framework leads to better outcomes compared to various baseline
methods.  Furthermore, we observe that the few-shot setting produces more accurate
sentiment predictions than the unsupervised approach for translating comments from
Hindi to English.  To facilitate future research, we have made the dataset and code
publicly available at this link: https://github.com/shravanku99/MT-Sentiment.

This study reveals intriguing evidence of a complex internal differential rotation within a Ultra-Short Period (USP) candidate, showing a rapid surface rotation of 2.6 km/s for a brown dwarf or heavy planet that disheveled its accretion disk and became a true USP.  The discovery that this massive companion, likely a 25$^{th}$ Mass Sun Jupiter, was not already spinning this fast, suggested angular momentum redistribution mechanisms, such as tidal forces, could produce such extreme rotations in existing or future USP systems.  The team analyzed high-cadence X-ray timing data from a observation session, revealing a complex variation in spin-up trends, possibly caused by tidal forces, and identified a sharp increase in rotation acceleration within a specific frequency range, indicating a turbulent internal state, possibly caused by rotational instability, within the companion.  The research results were valuable for understanding the formation and evolution of USP systems and might have helped explain the origin of detectable surface velocities in systems with highly disordered angular momentum.

The rapid proliferation of social media has given way to deceptive content that exploits the visual and engaging nature of multimedia posts. While existing methods have attempted to detect such misinformation, their effectiveness is often limited when confronted with large volumes of training data. In response, our proposed framework, MEAD, aims to tackle the challenge of detecting deceptive news with an emphasis on learning from limited examples. By incorporating the power of meta-learning and processing data in real-time without the need for extensive annotation, MEAD achieves state-of-the-art results in performance. According to studies on Weibo and Twitter datasets, our framework outstands other competing frameworks with 8.6% and 10.02% improvements respectively.

This research presents designs for constructing multi-component systems consisting of sequence sets, where in a multi-level format, each component is assigned a distinct phase value at specific locations. These systems, extending the concept of Golay complementary pairs, are relevant in image reconstruction technologies like holographic and radar imaging. At this multi-dimensional level, a ideal format ensures that combined correlation characteristics exhibit no side lobes. However, achieving these ideal standards is challenging in many situations. To address this, we introduce efficient methods for constructing systems that closely mimic the ideal features, where one approach leverages existing sequence sets with low side lobes and another builds upon mathematical structures known as complementary designs. Notably, our results demonstrate that large-scale multi-component systems with strong complementary properties can be constructed.

Following successive catastrophic events such as collisions or electrical malfunctions, robots experience injury requiring repair to continue operations. A key requirement for designing repair mechanisms is the precise identification and localization of injured areas. A critical challenge in developing repair designs lies in the difficulty of obtaining accurate models of injured robots' physical characteristics to design repair mechanisms. An possible solution involves a new model called Progressive Brain Injury Synthesis PAVIS comprising four primary components: A initial auto-encoder compressing high-dimensional data into lower dimensions; a modular injury generator introducing high-dimensional defects in specific areas; a damage-aware decoder processing injured data into physical characteristics; and a iterative injury amplifier progressively enhancing injury definitions in iterative cycles. Each component contributes uniquely to the overall model's efficacy. The auto-encoder reduces data dimensions; the injury generator creates high-dimensional defects; the decoder processes injured data; and the iterative mechanism improves injury definitions. Experimental results demonstrate that PAVIS outperforms existing models in injury simulation with scores of 0.83, 93.43%, 97.13% and 2D/4D injury recovery rates of 86.13%/83.13% and 101.11%/98.89% respectively, exceeding baseline approaches significantly. This new model paves the way for the design of repair mechanisms for catastrophic injuries requiring precise identification and localization of injured areas.

Presenting a collective framework of experimental results in a tabular format, we delve into the outcomes of multiple features used in enterprise anti-spam defense systems. Our analysis reveals that enterprise anti-spam systems utilize a variety of internal features for model training and deployment, underscoring the necessity of a unified representation model for effective research on enterprise data.

Recent advances in large language models have achieved human-like performance on numerous language tasks. However, the potential for these models to manipulate generated content in ways that promote fairness and prevent discrimination based on origin or identity has not been thoroughly explored. This research on a structured knowledge injection technique aims to eliminate bias in LLM outputs by systematically integrating accurate domain knowledge into the model's responses, rather than leaving it to the language model's training data. A randomized approach to presenting and formatting this integrated knowledge is used to prevent the model from developing an predictable pattern in its responses. This technique has been effectively demonstrated to override misleading information in the initial prompt and is found to be beneficial when used with optimized hyperparameters. To validate the significance of this knowledge injection technique, it is compared to conventional methods on multiple benchmark datasets and a newly created skill test suite. The structured knowledge integration approach is found to outperform traditional methods in all scenarios and is particularly beneficial in a knowledge-free initial training data environment. This research suggests that this technique can be used to impart a broad range of knowledge and abilities on LLMs in a fair and unbiased manner.

Non-linear electromagnetic fields impact both the optical depth and force balance within black hole accretion flows, potentially altering their overall dynamics, especially under extreme conditions. This research examines accretion processes on charged black holes in a de Sitter space environment, subject to an external electric field, to determine the conditions under which multiple stable shade levels can occur, noting that this phenomenon is influenced by the strength of the cosmic horizon and the black hole, as well as the intensity of the electric field, and can lead to limit-cycle behaviour. The research also establishes critical thresholds for the occurrence of multiple shade levels and limit cycles, and explores the relationship between these stable shade levels and the first-order phase transitions observed in Anti-de Sitter spaces, finding that they are closely connected, particularly in non-linear electromagnetic scenarios and under the influence of external fields, confirming the validity of the shade equivalence principle.

Following the details provided in Ref. 1, this article introduces a novel approach to constructing a quantum master equation for a driven-dressed system by applying the Wigner-Weyl representation combined with the GW approximation. To better understand the characteristics of the system, we utilize the quantum picture operation method (QPOUM) to derive the system's path integral propagator in phase space, specifically for light-matter interactions with a one-dimensional harmonic oscillator and a continuous drive. As a result, we can obtain the density matrix's time evolution operator and calculate both short-term coherence and long-term entanglement between the oscillator and the drive. To visualize the interactions, we utilize various representations, including the Wigner function and the parity-coherent state (PACS) tomogram, to illustrate the dynamics of the system.

Researchers have observed the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 K^0_S$ decay mode for the first time and have gathered more data on the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 K^{*0}$ and related decay modes. Using a 3.0 fb$^{-1}$ dataset of $bbbar$ pairs collected by the Belle II experiment at specific center-of-mass energies, researchers found the branching fraction of $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 K^0_S$ to be less than 1.7 x 10$^{-6}$ at the 90% confidence level. Additionally, they measured the branching fractions of $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 K^{*0}$ and $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0} K^{*0}$ decays to be (6.3±1.4±0.6±0.6) x 10$^{-5}$ and (7.1±1.6±0.7±0.6) x 10$^{-5}$, respectively.

Constructing the lattice of submodules of a given module is generally a challenging task. A promising solution exists for modules with unique decompositions, also known as multitype-free modules, by utilizing the information about the intersections of summands. This process involves constructing a bipartite graph where the nodes represent the summands, and the edges depict the relations between them. In this study, we extend the method beyond the full information about sub-lattices of summands, proposing an algorithm to construct the lattice of submodules given only the lattices of submodules for the summands. The effectiveness of this novel approach is demonstrated through several examples.

We explore how certain differential operators impact structures on tensors, focusing on their commutation relations and the derivation of specific identities. These developments enable us to investigate the behavior of certain types curvature vectors for hypersurfaces in Euclidean space. As a result, we prove that certain types curvature vectors's influence is minimal on the geometry of hypersurfaces in Euclidean space, showing that these vectors's effects lead to the recurrence of certain operators on specific tensor images in the process.

A subgroup within a free group of two generators is termed a cyclically uniform subgroup when its elements' representatives on the Davis-Gerard graph form a geodesic subgraph. Within this context, we develop an algorithm to construct the graph's ideal boundary's subgroup action on the subgraph's ideal boundary. Additionally, we characterize the subgroup's abelianization in terms of integer linear combinations of vectors.

The decay rate of $B_s^0$ into $D_s^{*-}\mu^+
u_{\mu}$ has not been observed yet, but it is thought to behave similarly to $B^0$ into $D^{*-}\mu^+
u_{\mu}$. To improve the prediction of this rare decay's rate, we conducted a shape analysis of the $B_s^0$ into $D_s^{*-}\mu^+
u_{\mu}$ form factors. Using data from $ ar{B}s$-factories, we achieved a slight enhancement over the current measurement, resulting in a weak signal observation of this specific decay rate.

A persistent puzzle in the field of self-organized criticality involves the functional form derived from the power spectrum of noise in systems that have reached a critical state. A recent study investigated the source of this power law behavior using a simple, mechanical system known for its noisy operation as it adheres to a surface and then detaches in a process called stick-slip motion. This particular investigation found that when analyzing the source of noise in a system consisting of a tape being peeled from a flat surface, a logarithmic spectrum results from a specific resonance within that system. However, by adjusting the peeling process to induce a constant rate of energy release, a power law behavior emerges in the resulting power spectrum.

In 1930, mathematician Menger developed an interest in the geometry of angle functions, which he considered to be generalizations of point geometries. He presented two specific theorems relating to this geometry but was unable to provide proofs for two particular examples he discussed. For nearly a century, these unresolved examples continued to puzzle the mathematical community until their resolution remained elusive. In an effort to address these unresolved cases, we first examined the fundamental characteristics of the angle function geometry. We recap the two problematic examples mentioned by Menger and then proceed to resolve them. Our findings demonstrate that the two initially problematic examples actually possess the same geometric properties as Euclidean spaces in two dimensions, satisfying a specific completeness condition first described by Blashke.

Point Cloud Models represented in histogram format are frequently utilized due to their efficiency, but they contain ambiguities that limit their expressive power. In an effort to address this issue and enable model sharing, a format-preserving encryption called TPC has been developed. Although TPC produces consistent encrypted representations suitable for use in point cloud networks, research found that it results in residual equivalence classes that are large in size. To tackle this problem, a new formatting method called Transformation-Unique Smoothing (TPSU) has been proposed. This smoothings technique is applicable to various model sizes and can significantly reduce the size of remaining equivalence classes, thereby enhancing the performance of point cloud networks for 3D object recognition tasks. Experiments were conducted on multiple datasets, demonstrating that TPCSU produces results comparable to existing encrypted formats while providing significant improvements in performance.

The integration of formal verification and testing techniques aims to provide improvements in both program testing geometry. Compiler-generated test data is considered to be analogous to geometric shapes, while successful execution of tests is viewed as the finding of intersections between these shapes. We have developed a geometry tool called PG-Test that allows for the proving of theorems and the generation of test data in an interactive manner. This tool has been used to verify the Coq-based typing theory for Java programs and to demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach by finding errors in tests and identifying types that are useful for error detection.

We provide a new proof of a result established by Clear in 2016, confirming that the diagonal representation of GL_2(2) has a non-vanishing property for wights associated with Kummer theory when the rank is at least 2. This specific result falls under the framework of Arthur-Crezberg theory.

To ensure the safe operation of advanced composite materials used in structural applications, real-time monitoring of their condition is essential. This paper proves the concept of precisely mapping damage patterns in a graphene epoxy composite under cyclic loading, utilizing genetic algorithms to optimize the interpretation of electrical data through electrical impedance tomography. A consistent correlation was found between applied stress and changes in electrical conductivity, exhibiting a linear relationship at low stresses and a non-linear pattern at higher stresses. However, traditional methods failed to accurately depict true damage distributions, often resulting in unrealistic images. In contrast, by optimizing the data collection process with genetic algorithms, a precise conductivity-concentration curve was established, allowing for the precise visualization of damage patterns across various load levels. This method also correctly predicted failure points and demonstrated hysteresis in response to cyclic loading, providing a reliable basis for structural health monitoring.

This work proposes a tensor framework for Euclidean space that relies on geometric concepts such as length, angle, and area, thereby eliminating the need for intricate theoretical explanations. By presenting a vector quantity as a first-rank tensor and a vector product as a second-rank tensor, we can derive a formula for the vector product of two vectors a and b as a third-rank tensor expression. Additionally, we can describe the vector product of three perpendicular vectors as a fourth-rank tensor, allowing us to calculate the dot product of two vectors as an operation involving a fifth-rank tensor. As a result, all vector operations in a 3-dimensional Euclidean space can be fully expressed in terms of geometric and tensor ideas, demonstrating the sufficiency of this approach.

If a right-angled Artin graph experiences a non-trivial splitting into components with finite relative isotropy, we demonstrate that this structure corresponds to a separation of the graph's vertices. This implies that additional relationships among the group's elements are identifiable and enforceable.

Iterative methods for matrix inversion have gained prominence due to their applicability in large-scale matrix computations, particularly with the surge in LDPreconditioning techniques for solving linear systems. Among these, GPU acceleration has become a key area of interest. Our research introduces generalized versions of existing GPU-accelerated matrix inversion methods, building upon a previous acceleration technique for solving linear systems proposed and optimized for GPU use. Generalizations include extending a fast iterative method, HM/inverse, to non-Hermitian matrices and developing new iterative techniques for both symmetric positive definite and general square matrices. Numerical results from experiments on large matrices demonstrate the effectiveness of the generalized approaches.

Contextual linear bandits is an effective framework addressing the decision-making problem in type of learning tasks where features are associated with inputs, including applications in areas of learning relevant to systems operating in contexts of learning environments. Given the importance of developing approaches suitable for systems operating in contexts of learning environments on hardware with limited capabilities and in settings with restricted information, the aim is to design contextually-based online learning algorithms that guarantee performance while utilizing minimal communication and memory resources. To this end, the paper proposes a new strategy for contextually linear bandit problems on distributed systems consisting of multiple agents sharing learning environments and demonstrates its efficacy through theoretical analysis and comparisons with existing methods.

A phenomenon observed in protoplanetary disks where the disk material shows rapid rotation towards the disk's edges has piqued our interest.  A theoretical model considering the evolution of grain size, along with a stability analysis incorporating a torque caused by dust clumping was created to investigate this issue.  Initially, a basic model of disk structure and rotation profile was developed to estimate the vertical shear instability (VSI) temperature range and the point at which emissions peak.  Subsequently, a more complex model integrating a radiative transfer equation and surface evolution equations for dust was created to determine the VSI stability with consideration given to the torque caused by dust clustering and the ultimate cause of rapid rotation profiles, particularly in the outer regions of disks.  Results indicate that the VSI temperature range and the point at which dust clustering torque becomes significant are influenced by the initial size of dust particles.  Larger dust particles lead to a narrower VSI range and an easier occurrence of dust clustering-induced shear instability.  Moreover, models with smaller initial dust particle sizes exhibit a more pronounced inward sloping of the rotation profile in the outer regions of disks compared to models with larger initial dust particles.  Inward-sloping rotation profiles contribute to the development of external instabilities, including the VSI, by a significant margin.  Overall, the evolution of grain size plays a crucial role in determining the stability of protoplanetary disks, with smaller particles contributing to a higher susceptibility to shear instability and a more pronounced inward-s

This research focuses on harmonic functions within the context of a certain class of manifolds where the Ricci curvature is positive and the scalar curvature is consistently decreasing. We have derived a key theorem demonstrating that only trivial (constant) harmonic functions exist under the given conditions, building upon an earlier result by Choi and Sakaguchi. As a result, we have identified the Euclidean space as the only steady gradient Ricci soliton that admits a non-constant harmonic function of a specific type.

Recent advancements in outsourcing training and machine learning as a service have created innovative threats such as hidden functionalities that are embedded in artificial neural networks. In typical research scenarios, triggers that activate these embedded features are static in their positioning and pattern, thus enabling detection mechanisms to function effectively. However, researchers have recently discovered methods like Neural Cleanse and ARD that are capable of implementing hidden functionalities that are dynamic, meaning they adapt based on the content of incoming data. This new approach presents challenges in detection and training and outputs limitations in functionality implementation. Yet, in our study, we introduce an optimization technique that integrates with existing outputs limitations, specifically global average pooling, to develop more effective functions that are implemented dynamically. Our results show that the proposed approach significantly enhances the accuracy of recognizing German hand gestures when used to train a ResNet10 model compared to typical methods, and also reduces the accuracy of detecting hidden functionalities by only 10%. Furthermore, our technique demonstrates its capacity to personalize the functionality implemented based on various input conditions, thus showcasing its adaptability.
